neighbours.label: the word just before a verdict that an idea is impossible or absurd ('is nearly [impossible]', 'would have seemed [absurd]'), as against the same words before an ordinary description
fire: Getting a reservation there on a Friday night is nearly impossible.
Twenty years ago this would have seemed a ridiculous idea.
Without a map, finding the cave in that forest is almost impossible.
To most doctors at the time, the theory would have sounded absurd.
Persuading the board to cut its own pay is next to impossible.
A decade earlier, such a merger would have seemed unthinkable.
Keeping a secret in such a small village is nearly impossible.
Back then, a phone without buttons would have seemed absurd.
quiet: Getting the new kitchen ready for Friday night is nearly done.
Twenty years ago this road would have taken a full day to drive.
Without a map, we reached the cave in that forest almost by noon.
To most doctors at the time, the patient would have looked healthy.
The board's office is next to the main entrance downstairs.
A decade earlier, the merger would have needed two signatures.
The new bakery in the small village is nearly open.
Back then, a phone without buttons would have cost a lot more.

predictions: fire 0.4-0.7 on 'nearly', 'would', 'seems' when the sentence sets up a judgment of impossibility or absurdity; the same words before neutral completions (nearly finished, would have arrived) below 0.2
